item.title: North Korea Fires Multiple Short-Range Ballistic Missiles
item.description: North Korea fired multiple short-range ballistic missiles toward its east coast Saturday, a day after the US, South Korea and Japan wrapped up joint military exercises that Pyongyang views as a threat to its security.
item.dc:creator: Myungshin Cho

item.title: Remembering 9/11, 25 Years Later
item.description: "Balance of Power" focuses on the intersection of politics and global business. On today's show, Ian Bremmer, President and Founder of Eurasia Group and GZERO Media, says disruptions to Saudi Arabia’s East-West pipeline and the Houthis’ ability to threaten the Bab el-Mandeb Strait illustrate how weaker regional powers can gain leverage through disruption. Michael Duffey, Under Secretary of Defense for Acquisition and Sustainment, says that AI offers tremendous potential for the department, but says funding is essential to rebuilding the defense industrial base. Fred Wellman, Democratic Candidate for Missouri's Congressional 2nd District and a US military veteran of Iraq, says Missouri’s redistricting fight created confusion for voters and discusses his campaign’s effort to reach voters across the district following the court decision. (Source: Bloomberg)

item.title: DOJ Ramps Up Controversial Probe of Trump’s Perceived Enemies
item.description: The US Justice Department is ramping up a controversial investigation into whether former government officials years ago conspired to undermine President Donald Trump, according to people familiar with the matter.
item.dc:creator: Chris Strohm and Jimmy Jenkins

item.title: Core CPI Hikes Ahead of FOMC Meeting
item.description: A key gauge of US consumer prices rose by more than expected last month, bolstering the case for Federal Reserve officials to raise interest rates next week. Bloomberg Intelligence US Interest Rate Strategist Ira Jersey and Bloomberg News Marco Strategist Frank Monkam discuss how the oil market is moving and what it all means for the Fed ahead of its September meeting next week. Then, Kalshi Chief Risk Officer Udesh Jha talks about the prediction market platform launch of Gold & Silver perpetual trading. Plus, the 2026 NFL season kicked off this week. Bloomberg News Senior Reporter and Co-Host of the 'Business of Sports' Podcast Randall Williams previews the season. All on the latest episode of "Bloomberg Businessweek Daily." (Source: Bloomberg)

item.title: Wellman on Missouri Voters Face Redistricting Showdown
item.description: Fred Wellman, Democratic Candidate for Missouri's Congressional 2nd District and a US military veteran of Iraq, says his time as an Army reservist shaped his view of the burden of leadership as the country marks 25 years since 9/11. Wellman says Missouri’s redistricting fight created confusion for voters and discusses his campaign’s effort to reach voters across the district following the court decision. Wellman discusses his strategy for competing in the congressional race despite a significant fundraising gap with his opponent. He speaks with Tyler Kendall on Bloomberg’s "Balance of Power." (Source: Bloomberg)

item.title: Pentagon’s Top Weapons Buyer Says Congress Must Act on Munitions
item.description: A top Pentagon official said lawmakers must “step up and deliver” on the Trump administration’s $1.5 trillion funding request if the military is to replenish its stockpiles of key air defense interceptors and deep-strike weapons that have seen heavy use in the Iran war.
item.dc:creator: Courtney McBride and Tyler Kendall

item.title: Sec. Duffey Says Pentagon Needs Funds to Rebuild Munitions
item.description: Michael Duffey, Under Secretary of Defense for Acquisition and Sustainment, says that AI offers tremendous potential for the department, but says funding is essential to rebuilding the defense industrial base. Sec. Duffey says the Pentagon is focused on increasing production of critical munitions including Patriot, Tomahawk and Standard missiles and argues that longer-term contracts can encourage industry to expand capacity. Sec. Duffey also says defense companies need to prioritize production and the war fighter when considering stock buybacks and dividends. He speaks with Tyler Kendall on Bloomberg’s "Balance of Power." (Source: Bloomberg)

item.title: Billionaire Delo Gives Record £36 Million to Farage’s Reform UK
item.description: BitMEX founder Ben Delo pledged £36 million ($48.7 million) to Nigel Farage’s Reform UK, a record donation designed to help the insurgent party fend off its critics while turbo-charging its attempts to gain power at the next general election.
item.dc:creator: Alex Morales

item.title: Bremmer Says Iran’s Leverage is Real but Will Diminish
item.description: Ian Bremmer, President and Founder of Eurasia Group and GZERO Media, says disruptions to Saudi Arabia’s East-West pipeline and the Houthis’ ability to threaten the Bab el-Mandeb Strait illustrate how weaker regional powers can gain leverage through disruption. Bremmer says Iran’s leverage is substantial today, but thinks countries will build greater resilience over time, reducing their exposure to Tehran. He speaks with Tyler Kendall on Bloomberg’s "Balance of Power." (Source: Bloomberg)

item.title: Claude Misused for Weapons Research
item.description: On the latest episode of the early edition of Balance of power, David Gura and Christina Ruffini speak with Mike Shepard, Bloomberg Senior Editor for Technology and Strategic Industries; Rick Davis, Partner at Stonecourt Capital and Bloomberg Politics Contributor & Jeanne Sheehan Zaino, Democracy Visiting Fellow at Harvard Kennedy School's Ash Center and Bloomberg Politics Contributor. They also speak with Nicholas Burns, former US Ambassador to China and NATO, and Brigadier General Leland Blanchard II, Interim Commanding General of the District of Columbia National Guard. (Source: Bloomberg)

item.title: How Larry Ellison Built His Empire
item.description: Expanding from database software into artificial intelligence and media, Larry Ellison is placing his biggest bets yet. Bloomberg Originals explores what drives the 82-year-old tech billionaire. (Source: Bloomberg)

item.title: Inflation Rises, Wealth Transfers, Case For Social Security | Bloomberg Money 9/11/2026
item.description: Bloomberg Money takes the pulse of your financial life, powered by the reporting of our global newsroom. Today's guests: Centerview Partners Senior Counselor, Council on Foreign Relations President Emeritus, and Former Advisor to Colin Powell & President H.W. Bush Richard Haass and Morgan Stanley Wealth Management Chief Economic Strategist Ellen Zentner. (Source: Bloomberg)

item.title: Hot US Inflation Pushes Fed Toward Rate Hike That Trump Opposes
item.description: Odds of a rate increase at next week’s meeting have shot up.
item.dc:creator: Catarina Saraiva

item.title: US Debt Is a National Security Issue, Haass Says
item.description: Richard Haass, senior counselor with Centerview Partners, president emeritus for the Council on Foreign Relations, and former advisor to Colin Powell and President George H.W. Bush, says America's $40 trillion national debt, is not just a fiscal problem but a national security concern. He speaks with Scarlet Fu on "Bloomberg Money." (Source: Bloomberg)

item.title: Canada’s Insurance Policy Against Trump
item.description: Is Canada becoming the EU’s 28th state rather than the US’ 51st? That’s more meme than reality, but they are building a hedge against America, says Bloomberg Opinion columnist Lionel Laurent. (Source: Bloomberg)

item.title: Some 9/11 Families Use Ceremony to Push Trump on Saudi Arabia
item.description: Some family members of those killed on Sept. 11, 2001, used the 25th anniversary ceremony to call on President Donald Trump to hold Saudi Arabia accountable for its alleged complicity in the US’s worst terrorist attack.
item.dc:creator: Sonya Dymova

item.title: Trump’s ‘Golden Age’ Confronts Economic Angst That Threatens GOP
item.description: The Republican faithful, gathered in arena hallways and hotel ballrooms during this week’s midterm convention, projected confidence they had a good story to tell on the economy.
item.dc:creator: Josh Wingrove

item.title: India Hosts BRICS Leaders' Summit 2026
item.description: India is hosting the BRICS leaders’ summit in New Delhi over the weekend, bringing together leaders from major emerging economies. Bloomberg's Haslinda Amin is in Mumbai with a preview of what to expect. (Source: Bloomberg)

item.title: Houthi Gains Leave MBS With Few Good Options in Yemen
item.description: As the Iran-backed Houthis gain ground in Yemen and strike Saudi Arabia’s oil infrastructure, the kingdom faces a stark choice: escalate a military campaign that’s for years failed to defeat the militants or tolerate greater rebel leverage over a Red Sea route that’s become increasingly important to its oil exports.
item.dc:creator: Simon Marks, Peter Martin and Veena Ali-Khan

item.title: Burnham’s EU Reset Under Pressure After Bloc’s Canada Deal
item.description: UK Prime Minister Andy Burnham was just weighing his first careful steps toward a reset with the European Union when he got lapped on the road to Brussels by Canada’s Mark Carney.
item.dc:creator: Chloe Chaplain, Alberto Nardelli, Ania Nussbaum and Alex Wickham
